messages:
Cal: Heads-up — found raw x-request-id values in traced attributes sent to Honeycomb from the node onboarding sample when LOG_LEVEL=trace + OTEL_PROPAGATE_HEADERS=1. This is a PII leak in traces. :(
Mei: Whoa. Can you repro? We thought redaction masks headers before export.
Cal: Repro is simple on my laptop. Clone sampleapp, set `LOG_LEVEL=trace OTEL_PROPAGATE_HEADERS=1 REDACT_SENSITIVE=true`, start, then hit endpoint a few times. Traces show `http.request_id` attribute with the unmasked GUID.
Sanjay: Quick theory: otelHook grabs header values into span attributes during request start, but our redaction middleware runs later (it mutates headers before logging). So traces get the pre-redaction value.
Cal: Minimal repro snippet (order matters):
```js
app.use(telemetry.otelHook()) // attaches header attrs to span early
app.use(telemetry.redactHook()) // masks headers for logs
app.use(telemetry.logHook())
```
Cal: I intentionally set LOG_LEVEL=trace to force extra attribute copy. The telemetry exporter shows `http.request_id: "8f3a-...-9b"` in spans.
Mei: Hmm. We assumed redaction is the single-source-of-truth and would run before anything that exports PII. Looks like otelHook was optimized to run as early as possible.
Sanjay: Looking at code: otelHook currently calls `span.setAttribute('http.request_id', req.headers['x-request-id'])` on request start, synchronously. redactHook is a later middleware that calls `maskHeader(req.headers, 'x-request-id')`. So ordering causes leak.
Cal: Repro steps I used: `git checkout onboarding/sample-node@main && LOG_LEVEL=trace OTEL_PROPAGATE_HEADERS=1 REDACT_SENSITIVE=true npm run dev`, then `seq 1 3 | xargs -I{} curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/text -d '{"q":"x"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'`, then check spans in local OTLP collector UI.
Mei: Two clear fixes: 1) ensure redactHook runs before otelHook in sampleapps/SDKs, or 2) change otelHook to read header values from a canonicalized/redacted header accessor rather than raw req.headers. Option 2 is safer globally.
Sanjay: Another option: otelHook could defer copying header attributes until after redaction Promise resolves, but that increases latency/complexity. We should prefer deterministic redaction correctness over micro-optimizing early attribute capture.
Cal: For onboarding UX I'd prefer a low-risk immediate mitigation: update sampleapp to mount redactHook before otelHook and add a note in docs. Then follow up with SDK-level fix so users don't have to reorder.
Mei: Agreed. Also add an assertion in our CI that exported spans do not contain values matching the request-id regex when REDACT_SENSITIVE=true. Will prevent regressions.
Sanjay: I'll open a PR with two commits: (A) small sampleapp change that reorders middleware for hosted samples + doc note, (B) SDK patch that changes otelHook to call `getCanonicalHeader(req, 'x-request-id')` which returns redacted/masked value when REDACT_SENSITIVE is enabled. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/232
Cal: I also attached a small failing unit that simulates the interleaving and asserts attr is masked.
telemetry-bot: New issue TW-7001 created: "node sdk: span attributes leak raw x-request-id when OTEL_PROPAGATE_HEADERS + REDACT_SENSITIVE" — linked to PR #232.
onboard-bot: Heads-up: pause hosted node sample deployment until TW-7001 low-risk mitigation lands.
Mei: Nice catch, Cal. Let's get the sampleapp change merged quickly, add the CI assertion, then ship the SDK patch behind a minor release. Also add a short note in the telemetry FAQ about recommended middleware ordering.
Sanjay: Will add feature flag guard in SDK for Private deployments that prefer minimal startup overhead; flag defaults to safe redaction-aware mode.
Cal: Thanks everyone — I'll add the Honeycomb span examples and exact collector payloads to TW-7001. :coffee:
